question.prompt: A box contains \(28\) red balls, \(20\) green balls, \(19\) yellow balls, \(13\) blue balls, \(11\) white balls, and \(9\) black balls. What is the minimum number of balls that must be drawn from the box without replacement to guarantee that at least \(15\) balls of a single color will be drawn?

solutions.title: Find the largest draw that fails
solutions.explanation:
Find the largest possible draw that still avoids having \(15\) balls of any color.

Such a draw can contain at most \(14\) each of red, green, and yellow. It can contain all \(13\) blue, \(11\) white, and \(9\) black balls, since none of those colors has \(15\) balls available. Therefore any draw avoiding \(15\) of one color has at most
\[
14+14+14+13+11+9=75
\]
balls.

Taking exactly those amounts is possible, so \(75\) draws do not guarantee success. A draw of \(76\) balls exceeds this bound and must include at least \(15\) of one color.

The minimum is \(\boxed{76}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
